findings.title: Backup-code login skips the password check when any totpCode is sent
findings.body: The password check is gated on `user.password && !credentials.totpCode`. Any non-empty totpCode makes the whole password verification block get skipped. The new backup-code branch (line 131) runs regardless of the password, so a request with the email, a valid backup code, and any non-empty totpCode logs in without a password. The login UI clears totpCode in backup mode, so normal use is unaffected, but the credentials callback is reachable directly. The consequence is that a backup code, which is meant to be a second factor, becomes a standalone login credential. A leaked backup-codes download is enough to take over the account. The same gate already lets email plus a valid TOTP skip the password, and this PR extends that bypass to the new code path. The password must be verified independently of which second factor is used.

findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, allowing reuse and resurrection of codes
findings.body: The codes are read in the findUnique at the top of authorize (line 73), checked with indexOf, and then the entire array is written back here. There is no transaction, row lock, or conditional update. Two concurrent logins presenting the same code both pass the check and both succeed, so one code can be spent twice. Two logins presenting different codes race as well: the later write overwrites the earlier one with a stale array, which restores the first code as valid again. Consumed codes can therefore come back to life. The update should be conditional on the value that was read (for example updateMany where backupCodes equals the value read, retrying on mismatch), or run inside a transaction with a row lock.

findings.title: Backup codes are unreachable on the external TOTP screen (IdP/redirect login)
findings.body: The 'Lost access' button exists only in TwoFactorFooter. When totpEmail is set, which the signIn callbacks produce via loginWithTotp for accounts with 2FA, footerText uses ExternalTotpFooter, which offers only Cancel. The BackupCode screen therefore cannot be reached for those users, so the backup codes feature does not work for them. Even if the button were added, the identityProvider guard in next-auth-options.ts (line 113) rejects non-CAL accounts when totpCode is empty, so the backend would also need changing. The feature should either be offered on that screen with the backend path fixed, or the gap should be documented.

findings.title: Dismissing the dialog on the backup codes step permanently loses the codes
findings.body: The Dialog's onOpenChange is passed straight through (line 166). On the DisplayBackupCodes step, Escape, an outside click, or the close icon dismisses the dialog with no warning, and onEnable is not called. By this point the enable endpoint has already succeeded, so 2FA is active on the server. The codes are stored only encrypted, and no endpoint returns them again, so the user ends up with 2FA on, no copy of the codes, and the parent never notified. Their only way out is to disable 2FA. Guard onOpenChange on this step, or treat dismissal like the Close button, and tell the user on this screen that the codes will be shown only once.

findings.title: missing_backup_codes tells users to generate codes in settings, which is not possible
findings.body: The message reads 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' Nothing in this PR provides a settings UI or endpoint to generate backup codes. They are created only during the 2FA setup flow, and disabling 2FA clears them. Users who enabled 2FA before this change, or whose codes were cleared, are sent to do something that cannot be done. The text should describe a real recovery path, or regeneration should be added.

findings.title: Unrelated tabIndex=-1 on the shared PasswordField visibility toggle
findings.body: The show/hide password button now has tabIndex={-1}. PasswordField is shared by every password input in the app (login, signup, password change), not only the 2FA flow, and this change is unrelated to backup codes. It removes the toggle from keyboard tab order, so keyboard-only users can no longer reveal a password they are typing. Either drop the change or justify and scope it separately.

findings.title: The new backup-code login path has no test coverage
findings.body: The PR's own test plan step 2 (log in via 'Lost access' with a backup code) has no e2e or unit test. The TODO on this line acknowledges the gap. The authorize backup branch in next-auth-options.ts and the backup branch in disable.ts are also untested, which is how the password-gate bypass above went unnoticed. At minimum the tests should cover: a backup code logs in once, a second use is rejected with IncorrectBackupCode, a wrong code is rejected, and a backup code without the password fails.
